reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 28 question-paper pages and PDF pages 1–29 of the combined Higher Level scheme (cover, notes, contents, the Paper 1 scale table on page 4, the summary of mark allocations on page 5, the annotation notes on pages 6–7, every Paper 1 model solution and marking note on pages 8–28, and the Paper 2 title page 29). Each task boundary is the published scale beside its model solution, cross-checked against the printed summary.
sourceNotes: The paper is 300 marks: candidates answer all nine questions (Section A Q1–6, 25 marks each; Section B Q7 45 marks, Q8 50 marks, Q9 55 marks). Every question is retained.
35 independently marked units, matching the printed summary of allocations on scheme page 5. Q9(b)(i) and (ii) share one 15D scale (“(b)(i)+(ii)”) and are one task.

Paper 1 bands from the 2019 scale table on scheme page 4, which differ from later years: 5B 0,2,5; 5C 0,2,3,5; 10C 0,4,7,10; 10D 0,4,5,8,10; 15D 0,4,7,11,15. Every part prints the same ladder beside its scale.

This paper had no authored cards before this review; all 35 units are new. Marking points are lifted line by line from the scheme (read through the glyph repair map) and labelled with the part of the scheme they come from; Q5(a) and Q6(a)(i) keep each printed method’s ladder separately. Tables in prompts carry the printed values with blanks for the cells the candidate fills.
The question booklet is LC003ALP100EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003ALP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 2. All page references are PDF positions, which match the printed scheme page numbers.

cards.stem: The closed line segment [0, 1] is shown below. The first three steps in the construction of the Cantor Set are also shown: Step 1 removes the open middle third of the line segment [0, 1] leaving two closed line segments (i.e. the end points of the segments remain in the Cantor Set); Step 2 removes the middle third of the two remaining segments leaving four closed line segments; Step 3 removes the middle third of the four remaining segments leaving eight closed line segments. The process continues indefinitely. The set of points in the line segment [0, 1] that are not removed during the process is the Cantor Set.
